subject: land snail
title: This Snail Doesn't Hide From Beetles. It Clubs Them With Its Shell

scenes.text: Most snails hide when attacked. This one fights back.
In Hokkaido, Japan, snail-eating ground beetles hunt big land snails.
Related snails pull into their shells and wait for the attack to stop.
This one swings its whole shell like a club, knocking the beetle over until it gives up.
Its shell has a much bigger opening, with room for stronger swinging muscles.
A snail in Russia evolved the same move separately. Twice, a shell became a weapon.

description:
Two land snails, Karaftohelix gainesi in Hokkaido and Karaftohelix selskii in Russia's Far East, defend themselves against snail-eating ground beetles by swinging their shells like clubs and knocking the beetles over.
Close relatives withdraw into their shells instead. The swingers have bigger shell openings, and DNA shows the behavior evolved independently twice.
Which animal has the most surprising weapon?
first_comment: Another Japanese snail is known to club firefly larvae with its shell. Would you have guessed snails could fight?
